body:
How to learn AI by building something you love: I built 3 things and none of them started with "I should learn AI."
1. Atlaria, my travel social app
2. A tracker for my card collection
3. A website for my favourite gelateria
Start with the thing you care about (finance, fashion, football) and build for that. You push through the hard parts when it matters to you.
I'm Manraj Sidhu, AI developer, and this is how I actually learned.
Comment BUILD and tell me what you would make. I'll reply with where I would start.
guide: Build a small app or site around something you already care about, using an AI coding assistant to do the heavy lifting. You need ChatGPT (Codex) or Claude Code, plus a free Vercel account and, if the app stores data, a free Supabase project.
1. Pick one thing you care about (travel, a collection, a local shop, your money, your wardrobe) and write one sentence on what the app should do for it.
1. List the two or three screens or features that sentence needs, and drop everything else.
1. Ask ChatGPT (Codex) or Claude Code to scaffold the app with those screens and run it on your computer.
1. If the app needs to remember things, such as a card collection or user posts, create a Supabase project and ask the assistant to connect it and create the tables.
1. Add one feature at a time and check it works before asking for the next, for example showing what each card in your collection is worth.
1. Publish it on Vercel so you can open it on your phone and share the link.
1. When you get stuck, paste the exact error message back into the assistant and ask it to explain the cause before it changes anything.
Watch out: do not start from "I should learn AI". Start from something you care about, because that is what keeps you going through the hard parts.

```
You are my coding assistant. Help me build a small <web app or website> for <the thing I care about, for example my card collection, a local gelateria, travel plans>. I am <a beginner / have some coding experience> and I have <ChatGPT (Codex) or Claude Code>, a free Vercel account and <a Supabase project, or no database yet>.
The app should do this one thing: <one sentence describing the main job>. Start with only these screens or features: <screen or feature 1>, <screen or feature 2>, <screen or feature 3>. Do not add anything else yet.
Constraints: keep the code simple and explain each step in plain English. Use a common stack such as Next.js. Store data in Supabase only if the app needs to remember things, and keep any keys out of the code by using environment variables. Build one feature at a time and tell me how to check each one works before moving on.
Return: the project structure, the commands to run it on my computer, the code for the first feature, and the steps to publish it on Vercel.
```
